title: Patch: the pool probe rotates the AI, server and tools suites too, not only the cards' tests
thread:
**Issue #4249 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4249: Patch: the pool probe rotates the AI, server and tools suites too, not only the cards' tests
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Every game starts by dealing decks out of the shared card pool, and adding a single card to the pool shifts every random deal after it. There is a daily check that re-runs the card tests with every pool rotated one place, so it catches tests that secretly depend on exactly where a random deal lands before the next new card breaks them. But the practice-AI tests, the server tests and the developer-tools tests deal out of the same pools, and they never get that treatment. Once this is built, they do: the same daily rotation runs over those three suites, and any test that fails only because the pool moved gets rewritten so it no longer depends on the pool's order. Players notice nothing directly. The maintainer notices the next time a new card joins the game and the daily run stays green in suites nobody had ever probed.

## Why

- One more card in a pool moves every draw from it (R380). The rotation feature exists exactly for this: under it every pool the catalog query returns is shifted one place, and the documented fixes are to read a pool under a zero shift for content/order tests, or to search for the roll (or build the position directly) for roll tests (`crates/engine/src/testkit/pool_probe.rs` header).
- The hand script says it all: `scripts/pool-probe.sh` runs the suites that draw from real cards (`jackioh-cards`, `jackioh-ai`, `jackioh-server`, `jackioh-tools`) under the rotation feature, and its header admits no workflow runs it and only the cards' share runs daily.
- The daily test (`crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs`, about five minutes) builds and runs only `-p jackioh-cards`. The per-PR cover is only the engine's rotation canary, which keeps the rotation itself working, not any suite's tests.
- The other three suites really do draw from the live pools: the AI's deck builder deals from a catalog query over every set (`crates/ai/src/deck.rs`), the server's actor and duos engines and their tests deal real decks (`crates/server/tests/actor/engine_real.rs` deals seeded decks from the deckable pool), and the tools' arena, gate and fuzz waves deal from the same pools.
- Precedent: the cards-only probe already paid off twice (the daily-probe issue and the 22 failing card tests that had to stop depending on where a roll lands). The same breakage class is sitting unprobed in three more suites, and it will surface at the worst moment: the pull request that next adds a card to a pool.

## Proposal

- Mirror the existing daily cards test with daily rotation coverage for the other three suites named in `scripts/pool-probe.sh`: add `#[ignore = "daily: ..."]` test(s) in `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs` that shell out to the same kind of rotated run for `jackioh-ai`, `jackioh-server` and `jackioh-tools` (same feature flag and opt-level config, same isolated target directory), generalizing the existing `failed`/`report` helpers so a failure names each suite's tests and both documented fixes.
- Time it first with the script's four-package command; if the three suites together threaten the daily tests job's hour, split them into one daily test per package so the log shows which suite broke.
- Convert every failure the first rotated run finds, using only the header's documented patterns (zero-shift reads for content/order tests; roll search or directly built positions for roll tests).
- Change nothing per pull request: the engine canary stays the per-PR cover, since full rotated suites do not fit the eight-minute job budget (as the script's header already states).
- Update `scripts/pool-probe.sh`'s header so it says what now runs daily and what is still by hand.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs` (new daily test(s), generalized failure report)
- `scripts/pool-probe.sh` (header docs only)
- Tests converted where the probe fails them, most likely under `crates/ai/src`, `crates/server/tests` and `crates/tools/src`
- SPEC: R380 and the deck-legal pool (SPEC §2.6); no spec or ruling text changes, since the probe guards an existing ruling

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A daily test runs the AI, server and tools suites with every random pool rotated one place and fails with a per-test report (naming each test and both fixes) when one leans on where a roll lands
- [ ] Every failure the first rotated run finds is converted to the documented patterns, so the rotated run passes
- [ ] Per-PR CI is unchanged: no new per-PR job, and the engine's rotation canary still passes per pull request
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools` passes, plus `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` (only if a converted test cites a ruling)
- [ ] The daily tests job still finishes inside its hour with the new coverage in it

## Size and risks

Medium (`difficulty:medium`): a small harness change plus a bounded number of mechanical test conversions. Main risk is volume: the cards' share needed 22 conversions, and the server suite is the largest of the three, so the first rotated run may find a pile of them; each conversion follows an already-documented pattern. Second risk is daily runtime (cards take about five minutes; the server and tools suites are heavier), mitigated by timing first and splitting one test per package if needed. Rejected alternative: running the rotated suites on every pull request, which the script's header already rules out on the eight-minute budget; daily is where this check lives.

---

Class: `checks` → `priority:low`; relabel to change it.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44655574825)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Daily rotation coverage for the three suites that deal from the live card pools but never get probed: `jackioh-ai`, `jackioh-server` and `jackioh-tools`. `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs` gains one `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` test per package that rebuilds that package's tests under `jackioh-engine/pool-probe` (every pool rotated one place, R380) and fails with a per-test report naming both documented fixes. Every failure the first rotated run finds is converted using only the header's patterns, so the rotated runs pass. Per-PR CI is unchanged.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs` | change | Generalize `PROBE`/`failed`/`report` to take a package and suite label; add `run_probe` helper; add three daily tests (functions below); update the per-PR report unit test |
| `scripts/pool-probe.sh` | change | Header comment only (lines 8–11): say the AI/server/tools suites now run daily via the tools probe tests; behavior untouched |
| Converted test files, named by the first rotated run | change | Only the files the probe fails; likely `crates/ai/tests/ai/deck.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/observe.rs`, `crates/server/tests/actor/engine_real.rs`, `crates/server/tests/actor/dealt_deck.rs`, `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs`, `crates/tools/src/arena.rs` / `gate.rs` / `fuzz.rs` — each conversion uses one documented pattern and nothing else |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `apps/`, `e2e/`, any `spec/` note (no ruling text changes; the probe guards existing R380). Governing spec: SPEC §2.6 (deckbuilding, the deck-legal pool) and R380 (`spec/rulings/R0380.md`: a pool naming no set draws from every set that ships, so one more card moves every draw).

## Steps

1. Re-read the contract: `crates/engine/src/testkit/pool_probe.rs` header (the only two legal conversions: read a pool's content/order under `with_pool_shift(0, …)` — `hold_pool_shift(0)` for async tests — or search the roll with `seed_where`/`cursor_where` (#848) or build the position directly), `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs` in full, and `scripts/pool-probe.sh`.
2. Time the new coverage first, before editing: run `cargo test -p jackioh-ai -p jackioh-server -p jackioh-tools --features jackioh-engine/pool-probe --no-fail-fast` and record wall time. Cards take about five minutes; the three together must leave the daily-tests job (`super.yml`, 60-minute timeout) headroom. If they threaten the hour, stop and report (raising that timeout is under `.github/`, which the bot may not change).
3. In `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs`, generalize without changing the cards probe's behavior: keep `failed()` as is (the `test <name> ... FAILED` format is suite-independent); change `report(stdout, stderr)` to `report(stdout, stderr, suite: &str, package: &str)` so it says `failed N of the {suite} tests` and the rerun hint reads `cargo test -p {package} --features jackioh-engine/pool-probe <name>`; keep the log-echo block but move it into `run_probe(package: &str, suite: &str)`, which builds `PROBE`-style args (`test -p {package} --features jackioh-engine/pool-probe --no-fail-fast --offline --color never` plus the same two `--config` opt-level lines and `--target-dir` the cards probe uses, so all four probes share one fingerprint and one `target/pool-probe` build) and asserts with `report(...)`.
4. Add three tests beside `every_cards_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated`, each calling `run_probe`: `every_ai_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated` (`-p jackioh-ai`, suite `"AI's"`), `every_server_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated` (`-p jackioh-server`, suite `"server's"`), `every_tools_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated` (`-p jackioh-tools`, suite `"tools'"`). Each carries `#[ignore = "daily: rebuilds the {suite} tests under the pool-probe feature and runs them; the engine's pool_probe canary keeps the rotation itself per pull request"]` — the `daily:` form is enforced per-PR by `daily_every_ignored_test_says_it_runs_daily` in `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`, and the reason must name the per-PR cover.
5. Update the per-PR unit test `the_report_names_every_failed_test_and_both_fixes` for the new `report` signature: pass a suite label, assert the message names the suite, still assert both fixes (`with_pool_shift(0, …)`, `seed_where`, `cursor_where`), the failed names, and the broken-build tail path.
6. Update `scripts/pool-probe.sh`'s header (lines 8–11) to say the cards', AI's, server's and tools' shares each run daily via the corresponding `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` test in `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs`, and that by-hand runs remain for reproducing a daily failure. Change no command.
7. Run each new probe alone: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test pool_probe <new test> -- --ignored --test-threads=1`, starting with AI. Collect every `FAILED` name from the report.
8. Convert each failure with exactly one documented pattern: content/order assertions read the pool under `with_pool_shift(0, …)` (copy `crates/ai/tests/ai/deck.rs:838`); pinned-roll assertions search with `seed_where`/`cursor_where` (copy `crates/ai/tests/ai/activate.rs:423` / `training_grounds.rs:307`) or construct the position directly; async tests use `hold_pool_shift(0)` plus the `thread_overrides`/`install` handoff (`pool_probe.rs` header, `installing_a_threads_overrides_carries_its_shift`). Never loosen a tolerance, change a seed to dodge the rotation, or mark anything non-daily `#[ignore]`.
9. Re-run the three rotated probes to green, then run the proof commands in **Tests** and **Done when**.

## Tests

- `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs`, `the_report_names_every_failed_test_and_both_fixes` (per-PR unit test, updated): asserts `failed()` parsing, suite label, both fixes, build-failure tail. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test pool_probe the_report_names_every_failed_test_and_both_fixes`.
- `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs`, `every_ai_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated` (new, daily): rotated `jackioh-ai` suite passes. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test pool_probe every_ai_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated -- --ignored`.
- Same for `every_server_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated` and `every_tools_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated`, each with its package's command.
- Each converted test file keeps its own existing tests as the proof (e.g. `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai deck::`, `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server actor::`), run both normally and under `--features jackioh-engine/pool-probe`.
- Proof commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` only if a converted test cites a ruling id.

## Done when

- [ ] Three daily tests exist, one per package, each failing with a report that names every failed test and both documented fixes.
- [ ] The first rotated run's failures are all converted with the documented patterns; all three rotated runs pass.
- [ ] No new per-PR job; the engine's `pool_probe` canary still passes per-PR; every `#[ignore]` reads `#[ignore = "daily: …"]`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass (`cargo jackioh spec check` if a ruling is cited).
- [ ] Timed run shows the daily-tests job still fits its hour; `scripts/pool-probe.sh` header describes the new daily coverage.

## Risks

- Daily runtime: the server/tools suites are heavier than cards'. Mitigation: time first (step 2), share one target dir and one opt-level fingerprint so the four probes compile once; parallel outer threads serialize on cargo's build lock, which is safe.
- Statistical tests (AI deck curve over seeds, arena/gate waves) may look probe-broken while merely seed-sensitive: convert by searching the roll, never by widening a tolerance — tolerances are named constants (CLAUDE.md rule 9) and checks are never weakened.
- `deckable_pool()` in `crates/server/tests/actor/engine_real.rs` slices catalog order directly, so it is rotation-sensitive by construction; expect it to need `with_pool_shift(0, …)` or a searched seed.
- `scripts/pool-probe.sh` is referenced by `scripts/ci-scope.sh`'s skip map: header-only change keeps that mapping valid.

## Open questions

None blocking. Conditional handoff: if step 2 shows the three rotated suites threaten the daily-tests job's hour, the only lever is the workflow timeout under `.github/`, which the bot may not change — report the measured times and hand that part to a person instead of scoping the probes down silently.
```
